NASA Earth Jukebox – Summary
NASA Earth Jukebox is an innovative project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its main aim is to transform real Earth observation and climate data into music and sounds. It uses NASA satellite images and environmental information, such as temperature, ocean conditions, vegetation, and natural events. By converting scientific data into sound, people can understand changes happening on Earth through both hearing and seeing. This project also supports visually impaired people by making Earth science more accessible and interactive. Overall, NASA Earth Jukebox combines science, technology, music, and creativity to help people understand and protect our planet. �

🌍 EARTH JUKEBOX – Project Details

1. Team Qualifications

* First-year B.E. Computer Science and Engineering students.

* Skills in research, creative thinking, teamwork, basic programming, video editing and visual design.

2. What We Use

* NASA Earth Science Data

* Natural sound recordings

* Scientific information and images

* Web development and multimedia tools.

3. Tools & Technologies

* HTML – Website structure

* CSS – Website design

* JavaScript – Interactive features

* Canva – Visual design

* CapCut – Video editing

* Python – Data processing (optional)

4. Project Description

Earth Jukebox is an interactive platform that brings together Earth's natural sounds, images and scientific information. It helps people understand natural phenomena such as ocean waves, wind, rain and storms through audio and visuals.

5. Our Goal

To make Earth science interesting, interactive and easy to understand through sound and technology.

6. Expected Impact

* Environmental awareness.

* Interactive science learning.

* Better understanding of Earth's natural phenomena.

7. Team Name

Victory Titans

Project Tagline: Don't Just See the Earth. Listen to the Earth.
